feedback.problem:
The number of subscribers $S=S(t)$ to a website $t$ months after a marketing campaign can be modeled by the differential equation

$$
\frac{\text{d}S}{\text{d}t}=kS
$$

where $k>0$ is the growth rate. If there were $12\,000$ subscribers initially, and $S(2)=15\,000$, calculate the value of the growth rate $k$ to the nearest percent.

$k≈$
{{field-1}}
$%$
feedback.worked_solution:
We model the number of subscribers using the differential equation

$$
\frac{\text{d}S}{\text{d}t}=kS.
$$

The solution to this equation is

$$
S(t)={S}_{0}\,{e}^{kt},
$$

where ${S}_{0}$ is the initial value.

We're told that there were $12\,000$ subscribers initially, so we have ${S}_{0}=12\,000.$

Therefore, the number of subscribers $S$ at time $t$ is

$$
S(t)=12\,000\,{e}^{kt}.
$$

Finally, to find the value of $k,$ we substitute $S(2)=15\,000$ into the equation above and solve for $k,$ as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}S(2) & =12\,000\,{e}^{k\cdot 2} \\ 15\,000 & =12\,000\,{e}^{2k} \\ {e}^{2k} & =\frac{15\,000}{12\,000} \\ {e}^{2k} & =\frac{5}{4} \\ \operatorname{ln}⁡({e}^{2k}) & =\operatorname{ln}⁡(\frac{5}{4}) \\ 2k & =\operatorname{ln}⁡(\frac{5}{4}) \\ k & =\frac{1}{2}\operatorname{ln}⁡(\frac{5}{4}) \\ k & ≈0.111\,6\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, $k≈11%,$ rounded to the nearest percent.
